item.title: Data Munging with Perl: Twenty-Five Years Later
item.description: Celebrating the quarter-century anniversary of the second edition of Data Munging with Perl, Dave examines how data formats and tools have evolved since 2001, from frail HTML::TokeParser to XML buzzwords to APIs, JSON/YAML and proper Unicode. Meanwhile, the essential UNIX filter model of linking small, targeted tools has not changed much, though it has been updated with modern Perl concepts like using v5.36 and lexical filehandles.
item.author: dave_cross

item.title: Perl v5.45.5 - Development Release
item.description: The newly development released Perl v5.45.5 emphasises a lot on improvements in regex based on trie and speed-ups in Aho-Corasick scanning including Boyer-Moore-Horspool skipping and case insensitive improvements in trie as well as cached lookups through isa and deterministic parser error messages. There are important bug fixes that solve the nesting lvalue substr buggy issues which originated from version 5.44.0, initialisation of ${^UTF8CACHE} in the new threads and flags in PL_sv_zero so that the serialisers can consider zero as a number rather than "0".
item.author: eric_herman

item.title: One Korean title, three different lengths: testing Unicode keys in Perl
item.description: Using the Korean title as a concise Test::More fixture, rillbyteonion57 explains the problem of handling text in Perl when code points, grapheme clusters, and UTF-8 byte lengths are not distinguished. The article provides a simple pattern for catalog searching where both the insertion and searching operations use normalisation via NFC while keeping the original strings intact. Additionally, he points out the common mistake of confusing utf8 and :encoding(UTF-8) in file I/O operations.
item.author: rillbyteonion57

item.title: Adventures in CPAN Distribution Installation
item.description: In his article, Rob examines the reason why .packlist files disappear every time a new version of CPAN is released when you set INSTALL_BASE. He reveals that the problem stems from ExtUtils::MakeMaker not properly understanding the SYSTEM SITEARCHEXP when it goes through the process of writing to INSTALLSITEARCH. He discusses the original debate about the status of packlists and details a recent PR concerning a fix to the matter of file pathfinding.
item.author: rob_lauer

item.title: Perl: An Exercise in Write-Only Programming
item.description: Jean-Luc Martel, has published a fun and entertaining article in which he discusses the features of Perl programming that can be very useful but may also make programming in this language rather difficult, such as: embedded regex code and stateful matching, coercion DWIM, tie, AUTOLOAD, typeglobs, and early cgi-bin days.
item.author: jean_luc_martel

item.title: Punk: Perl MVC compiled at boot
item.description: In this presentation you will dive into the Punk ecosystem: an open source MVC web framework with first class openAPI integration, template engine, job queue, json codec, non blocking data layer and http client all built on a highly optimised event-loop web server.
item.author: robert_acock
